dcts.name: The incentive flip
dcts.offer: T2 S$290 Shortlist Teardown (mid-funnel) -> T3 S$4,500 flat-fee advisory
dcts.copy_1:
Your flat sold in three weeks. The same agent went quiet the moment you started buying.

You felt the reason before you could name it: on the buy, the better your price, the less they earn.

A flat fee can't flip. See the maths on a real shortlist for S$290.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.copy_2:
Your flat sold in three weeks. The agent was a machine.

Then you started buying, and the same person went quiet.

You felt it before you could name it. On the sell side, a higher price pays them more. On the buy side, the better the deal they get you, the less they earn.

The incentive flipped. On a seven-figure decision you keep for a decade, the advice you most need is the advice they're paid not to give.

That is not bad luck. It is the structure.

There is one structure where it cannot happen: a flat fee. S$4,500, the same whether you buy a S$900k flat or a S$1.6m condo. No commission. No referral split. Nobody earns more when you spend more.

You overpaid once. You said never again.

See the analysis on one shortlist unit for S$290, before you commit to anything.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.cta: See the analysis on one shortlist unit for S$290, before you commit to anything.
dcts.angle_rationale: MP-01 already half-sees the wound. Their flat sold fast, then the same agent went quiet on the buy, and they felt the incentive flip before they had words for it. So we name the felt moment first, then hand them the mechanism: a flat fee is the one structure where the advisor cannot earn more when they spend more. Lead with the problem they live, introduce the flat fee as the named fix, prove it with checkable numbers, not adjectives. Contrast the fee structure, never the people. Buying emotion is relief, not opportunity.
dcts.why_am_i_testing_this: Tests whether naming the buy-side incentive flip plus a clean flat-fee mechanism beats commission-agent aspiration copy for a scarred L4 upgrader who has already overpaid once.

dcts.name: Free isn't free
dcts.offer: T2 S$290 Shortlist Teardown (mid-funnel) -> T3 S$4,500 flat-fee advisory
headline_drafts: The cost you never see itemised
dcts.copy_1:
S$4,500 for advice, when agents are free? That's the reflex. It's also the trap.

The free agent isn't free. The commission is baked into the price you pay. You just never see it itemised.

One flat fee, shown to you. See the method on your shortlist for S$290 first.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.copy_2:
S$4,500 for advice, when agents are free? That's the reflex. It's also the trap.

The free agent isn't free. Their commission is built into the price you pay. You just never see it itemised. One quiet purchase later, most buyers work that out the hard way.

Here is the maths laid bare. A flat S$4,500, paid once, with the full analysis shown to you. Against a commission you can't see, on an incentive that rewards a higher price.

If a clear set of eyes stops you overpaying by even S$30k, the flat fee isn't the cost. It is the saving.

And you don't take it on faith. The S$290 Shortlist Teardown shows you the method first: a verdict on each unit, the numbers behind it, no pitch about how experienced anyone is.

Then you decide.

https://meridianpropertyadvisory.example.sg/advisory
dcts.cta: See the method on your shortlist for S$290 first.
dcts.angle_rationale: MP-03 decides on logic, not emotion. They are not blocked by paralysis or trust wounds. They are blocked by a pricing illusion: they think free is cheaper than S$4,500. Make the hidden commission visible and the math flips them fast. So we lead with the reflex objection ('free, why pay?'), expose the hidden cost, then reframe the flat fee as the cheaper, honest line item. Numbers they can re-run themselves. Contrast the structure, never the people. Anti-hype tone throughout because this buyer rejects outrage marketing as hard as they reject 'free'.
dcts.why_am_i_testing_this: Tests whether making the hidden commission visible converts the fee-allergic skeptic faster than emotional trust copy. Logical objection, logical answer.
